characterizations.result_summary: Observed homogeneous poly(MPC) polymer layer on substrate, surface roughness of 0.8~1.5 nm.

evidence.source_sentence: The AFM observation revealed that a homogeneous polymer layer was formed on the substrate, and the surface roughness was $0 . 8 \sim 1 . 5$nm in the dried state in a $5 \times 5 \mu \mathrm { m } ^ { 2 }$scanning area.

characterizations.result_summary: Measured adhesion and friction force of poly(MPC) brush in different solvents; observed strong interaction in poor ethanol/water solvent, low interaction in pure water, no significant salt concentration effect on adhesion properties.

evidence.source_sentence: Adhesion force (a) and friction (lateral) force (b) of poly(MPC) brush in a ethanol/water $( 7 0 / 3 0 , \boldsymbol { \mathrm v } / \boldsymbol { \mathrm v } )$ solution and NaCl aqueous solution measured by AFM using a colloidal probe cantilever with silica sphere $( d = 5 0 \ \mu \mathrm { m } )$ Friction force is represented by output of the photo diode at a scan rate of 10 $\mu \mathrm { m } / \mathsf { s }$ under normal load of 10 nN.
Figure 4 shows adhesion and lateral force for the high-density poly(MPC) brush surface measured by AFM using a colloidal probe in aqueous solution.

characterizations.result_summary: The thickness of poly(METAI) swelling brush remained unchanged in 1.0 M NaCl deuterium oxide solution.

evidence.source_sentence: Interestingly, quite similar reflectivity curve was observed from the interface of the poly(METAI) brush in the 1.0 M NaCl deuterium oxide solution, indicating that the thickness of the swelling brush did not change, even in a salt solution.
